title: Container Bookings: Dangerous-Goods Acceptances and the Late VGM Fee
content:
The dangerous-goods acceptances on a Container Bookings booking affect a late VGM entry in two separate ways: whether the free allowance is open, and how many containers the fee is charged on.

## Whether the allowance is open

Bookings of any cargo category other than dangerous goods always have the free allowance open. For a dangerous-goods booking the allowance opens only where the line has approved one or more of its acceptances for a container count greater than zero.

## Containers charged

The full late VGM fee is charged on the booking's container quantity reduced by the container count of its rejected dangerous-goods acceptance, never below zero; containers under a rejected acceptance never go on board, so no VGM is needed for them. With no rejected acceptance, the whole quantity is charged. A booking on which two or more acceptances have been rejected is not governed by these rules, which fix no container figure for it.

## Hypothetical cases

| Cargo category | Acceptances on the booking | Allowance open? | Containers charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| general | none | yes | full quantity |
| dangerous goods | one approved for 3 containers | yes | full quantity |
| dangerous goods | one approved for 3, one rejected covering 2, on a booking of 5 | yes | 3 |
| dangerous goods | one rejected covering 2, on a booking of 5 | no | 3 |

Acceptance status and container counts are read from the dangerous-goods acceptance records; the quantities here are invented.
